items.title: The Villages Health System $541.5 Million Settlement: A New Frontier in Medicare Advantage Risk Adjustment Enforcement - The National Law Review
items.reason: This item reports a major settlement involving Medicare Advantage risk-adjustment enforcement, which is a direct form of regulatory action and sanction against a healthcare entity relevant to payer enforcement.
items.summary: The Villages Health System agreed to a $541.5 million settlement with the federal government for alleged improper Medicare Advantage risk-adjustment practices. The settlement represents a significant enforcement action focused on how risk scores were calculated and submitted to CMS, affecting the reimbursement amounts the Medicare Advantage plans received. This case signals increased regulatory scrutiny of risk-adjustment coding and billing practices in Medicare Advantage, which directly impacts revenue-cycle operations for health systems submitting claims and negotiating with MA plans on reimbursement methodologies.
